stem:
Bharat has $60=2^{2}\times 3\times 5$ and $90=2\times 3^{2}\times 5$. He wants their HCF from these prime factorisations.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: Answer "common primes", naming that phrase instead of writing the HCF value.
Say that the HCF is what produces the shared primes, instead of reading the shared primes from the factorisations to build the HCF.
Keep only the common primes with the smaller count in each: $2^{1}\times 3^{1}\times 5^{1}=30$.
Report $60$, copying the smaller of the two given numbers because $60$ is printed first, without using the minimum powers.

teacher.key_rationale: HCF from prime factorisations keeps only primes that appear in every number, each raised to the minimum available power: here 2×3×5=30. Naming the phrase, reversing cause, or copying 60 miss that rule.
